claims.quote: The run on formal verification (2026-11-19) asks what Lion should add so a model can be proved correct, the way Alchemy's Verify proves its domain models with the Z3 solver. It weighs ten ideas against twelve programs on a bank account, in `research/probes/fv-*.json`, which show that Lion keeps invariants at every change and can search every sequence of commands up to a bound in plain code, but refuses any question about every value a variable could take. It ranks first a solver for the values a question leaves open, then bounded search with inputs drawn from schemas, then rules about what must eventually happen; proofs that every command keeps the invariants, invariant inference, and proof certificates build on the solver.
